long_biography.plain_text:
Military engineering shaped Vladislav Feliksovich Filev's approach to aviation. After graduating from the Mozhaisky academy, he served in the strategic missile forces before moving into industrial economics and investment management. In 1997 he joined Siberia Airlines' board as an investor representative. The following year he became chief executive as he and Natalia Fileva acquired control of the distressed carrier. They restructured its operations and developed it into the airline later branded S7.

Filev established S7 Group in 2005 to organise the airline and related aviation services under a holding company. He later moved from chief executive to board leadership as professional managers assumed daily operating titles. The ownership structure gave him 49.94% of the group and made him the principal influence over major decisions. The remaining shares were held by two other family shareholders. That equity and control structure does not make S7's aircraft, maintenance facilities, cargo operations or revenue his directly owned assets.

The Russian surname Филёв is more phonetically rendered Filyov and appears that way as an alias in formal records. Filev is retained as the primary English spelling because it is used consistently by Forbes, SEC filings and established English-language reporting.

Filev did not found the original Siberia Airlines. He became its board chairman and chief executive during the 1997-1998 acquisition, then founded S7 Group in 2005 around the transformed carrier.
